The IP addresses in the diagrams are illustrative. Actual subnets must avoid existing routes and have a configured gateway; macvlan may also restrict direct host-to-container communication. Support for host mode depends on the platform and Desktop settings. Published ports may bypass some normal host-firewall chains, so verify exposure against Docker's networking rules.

Volume storage paths depend on the daemon's data-root, rootless operation, the Desktop VM, and the driver. A bind mount hides existing content in the container's directory; it does not delete the image directory. Whether an empty volume is populated depends on the mount method and options such as nocopy. tmpfs data can also reach swap, so it is not guaranteed to be memory-only secret storage. --volumes-from only provides access; it does not produce a consistent backup. Databases require writes to be stopped, a snapshot, or a native backup procedure.
